<div class="sd-research" markdown="0">
<section class="sd-intro" aria-label="Research overview">
<p class="sd-eyebrow">Research vision</p>
<h2>From mathematical foundations to intelligent sensing and communications</h2>
<p>My research develops principled methods for extracting useful information from incomplete, noisy and structured measurements. I connect applied mathematics, statistical signal processing and optimization with sensing, wireless communications, privacy-aware inference, quantum computing and quantum sensing.</p>
<div class="sd-links"><a href="#research-directions">Explore research directions &darr;</a><a href="#funded-projects">Funded projects &darr;</a><a href="{{ '/publications/' | relative_url }}">Full publication list &rarr;</a><a href="{{ '/talks/' | relative_url }}">Talks &amp; slides &rarr;</a></div>
</section>
<h2 class="sd-section-title" id="research-directions">Research directions</h2>
<p class="sd-section-note">Ten connected themes, from the mathematics of inverse problems to future communication and sensing systems.</p>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Compressed sensing &amp; mathematical optimization</h3>
<p class="sd-question">What is the minimum information needed for reliable recovery?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">I study recovery guarantees, sample complexity and phase transitions for structured inverse problems, including weighted sparse and block-sparse recovery, total variation and dictionary-sparse models.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2019.2920640" title="DOI">On the Error in Phase Transition Computations for Compressed Sensing</a> <span class="sd-year">(2019)</span></li><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Measuring%20Less%2C%20Recovering%20More%3A%20Distribution-Aware%20Weighted%20%E2%84%93%E2%82%81%20Analysis%22" title="Scholar search">Measuring Less, Recovering More: Distribution-Aware Weighted ℓ₁ Analysis</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Low-rank recovery &amp; computational imaging</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can missing or blurred information be reconstructed?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">I develop prior-informed matrix sensing and completion methods, weighted nuclear-norm regularization and structured low-rank models for reconstructing signals and images from incomplete observations.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Multi-weight%20nuclear%20norm%20minimization%20for%20low-rank%20matrix%20recovery%20in%20presence%20of%20subspace%20prior%20information%22" title="Scholar search">Multi-weight nuclear norm minimization for low-rank matrix recovery in presence of subspace prior information</a> <span class="sd-year">(2022)</span></li><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Reconstruction%20of%20Binary%20Shapes%20from%20Blurred%20Images%20via%20Hankel-structured%20Low-rank%20Matrix%20Recovery%22" title="Scholar search">Reconstruction of Binary Shapes from Blurred Images via Hankel-structured Low-rank Matrix Recovery</a> <span class="sd-year">(2019)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Continuous-domain super-resolution &amp; blind inference</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can continuous parameters be recovered without a discretization grid?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">My work investigates atomic-norm methods, convex relaxation, blind deconvolution, demixing and multidimensional spectral estimation, including recovery from multiple measurement vectors and separation of radar signals from impulsive noise.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2025.3566885" title="DOI">Timely and painless breakups: Off-the-grid blind message recovery and users’ demixing</a> <span class="sd-year">(2025)</span></li><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Two-dimensional%20super-resolution%20via%20convex%20relaxation%22" title="Scholar search">Two-dimensional super-resolution via convex relaxation</a> <span class="sd-year">(2019)</span></li></ul></div>
<div class="sd-talk-links"><strong>Related talks &amp; slides</strong><a href="{{ '/talks/' | relative_url }}#offgrid-demixing">Off-the-grid blind deconvolution &amp; demixing slides &rarr;</a></div>
</div></article>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Near-field sensing, XL-MIMO &amp; ISAC</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can we sense and communicate using large antenna apertures?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">I develop continuous range-angle estimation and lifted super-resolution techniques for spherical-wave propagation, near-/far-field boundaries and collaborative integrated sensing and communications (ISAC).</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><span class="sd-award">IEEE SPAWC 2026 Best Paper Award</span> <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10234" title="arXiv">Living Off the Grid: Continuous Range-Angle Super-Resolution for Near-Field XL-MIMO</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31299" title="arXiv">A Mathematical Theory of Near-Field Super-Resolution</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.23919/WiOpt66569.2025.11123413" title="DOI">One target, many views: Multi-user fusion for collaborative uplink ISAC</a> <span class="sd-year">(2025)</span></li></ul></div>
<div class="sd-talk-links"><strong>Related talks &amp; slides</strong><a href="{{ '/talks/' | relative_url }}#nearfield-workshop">Near-field workshop (Kista) &rarr;</a><a href="{{ '/talks/' | relative_url }}#globecom-2025">GLOBECOM 2025 slides &rarr;</a><a href="{{ '/talks/' | relative_url }}#collaborative-isac">WiOpt 2025 collaborative ISAC slides &rarr;</a></div>
</div></article>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Massive MIMO &amp; channel dynamics</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can wireless systems adapt to evolving channels?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">I investigate spatial and temporal channel correlations, non-stationary Rician aging channels, channel estimation, pilot spacing, transmitter design and power allocation for multi-antenna communications.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Exploiting%20Spatial%20and%20Temporal%20Correlations%20in%20Massive%20MIMO%20Systems%20Operating%20Over%20Non-Stationary%20Aging%20Channels%22" title="Scholar search">Exploiting Spatial and Temporal Correlations in Massive MIMO Systems Operating Over Non-Stationary Aging Channels</a> <span class="sd-year">(2025)</span></li><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3490500" title="DOI">Toward Optimal Pilot Spacing and Power Control in Multi-Antenna Systems Operating Over Non-Stationary Rician Aging Channels</a> <span class="sd-year">(2025)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Massive access &amp; goal-oriented detection</h3>
<p class="sd-question">Can a network make the right decision without decoding everything?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">I explore blind and asynchronous activity detection, random access, joint channel estimation and task-oriented inference for large populations of connected devices, including stationary IoT applications.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/TSP.2023.3254140" title="DOI">Blind goal-oriented massive access for future wireless networks</a> <span class="sd-year">(2023)</span></li><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Enabling%20Massive%20Connectivity%20of%20Stationary%20IoT%20Devices%20via%202D%20Blind%20Goal-Oriented%20Detection%22" title="Scholar search">Enabling Massive Connectivity of Stationary IoT Devices via 2D Blind Goal-Oriented Detection</a> <span class="sd-year">(2025)</span></li></ul></div>

<h3>Semantic communications &amp; information privacy</h3>
<p class="sd-question">What should be transmitted, and what should remain private?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">My research examines task-relevant information transmission under privacy constraints, multi-task semantic communications, leakage bounds and privacy-preserving mechanism design.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Multi-task%20private%20semantic%20communication%22" title="Scholar search">Multi-task private semantic communication</a> <span class="sd-year">(2024)</span></li><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07523" title="arXiv">Sparse Point-wise Privacy Leakage: Mechanism Design and Fundamental Limits</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>

<h3>Communication-efficient distributed computing</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can multiple agents compute collaboratively with less communication?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">I study distributed computation using compressed sensing and matrix factorization, exploiting low-dimensional structure to reduce the information exchanged among computing nodes.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/ITW55543.2023.10160241" title="DOI">Multi-User Distributed Computing Via Compressed Sensing</a> <span class="sd-year">(2023)</span></li><li><a href="https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Communication-Efficient%20Distributed%20Computing%20via%20Matrix%20Factorization%22" title="Scholar search">Communication-Efficient Distributed Computing via Matrix Factorization</a> <span class="sd-year">(2024)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>

<div class="sd-card-content">
<h3>Quantum computing</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can quantum computation complement classical algorithms for estimation and optimization?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">An emerging research direction exploring quantum algorithms for signal processing and mathematical optimization, parameterized quantum circuits, hybrid quantum-classical methods, and quantum-assisted inference. I am interested in the mathematical foundations, computational trade-offs and practical limitations of these approaches.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Related research</h4><ul><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38500" title="arXiv">Q-SPARSE: Quantum Subspace Projection for Near-Field Angle-Range Spectrum Estimation</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>

<h3>Quantum signal processing &amp; sensing</h3>
<p class="sd-question">How can quantum representations support estimation and waveform design?</p>
<p class="sd-desc">My emerging research addresses quantum-assisted near-field angle-range spectrum estimation, subspace projection, operator uncertainty and cross-domain information in quantum signals.</p>
<div class="sd-papers"><h4>Representative publications</h4><ul><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38500" title="arXiv">Q-SPARSE: Quantum Subspace Projection for Near-Field Angle-Range Spectrum Estimation</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16049" title="arXiv">Operator uncertainty and cross-domain information in quantum signals: Second-moment bounds for quantum waveform design</a> <span class="sd-year">(2026)</span></li></ul></div>
</div></article>
</div>

<p class="sd-section-note">European collaborative research on future wireless and sensing systems.</p>
